verification_report.summary:
The full supplied reconstruction passes sequential verification under the stated accepted inputs. Both targets follow: continuous normalized existence with a strictly positive scalar, and continuous proper exponential existence for every fixed lambda>0, with uniqueness among bounded solutions. The audit covers all proof items, parameter dependencies and dimension n=1; it does not assess later zero-exponent consequences.

The local capacity test gluing is valid. The chosen delta is uniform over the finite cover and independent of each local test. The constant branch holds in a boundary collar, while on the smaller ball V=delta v+delta/2 and omega_V>=delta ddc v. Positivity therefore gives the claimed local-to-global capacity inequality, with the correct direction for the exponential volume bound. Cap(X)<infinity follows from local CLN applied only to tests in [0,1]. For the tail estimate, the negative quadratics make u+r_j nonpositive psh and v+r_j uniformly bounded psh; positivity and weighted CLN yield C(1+||u||_1)/t. Accepted normalized L1 control completes the argument. Holder and exponential decay then give the square capacity bound for all Borel sets, including capacity-zero sets.

The thin-sublevel argument has the correct shifted infima and strict inclusions: 0<=b=(1-epsilon)(w-v)<=t/2 implies m-t/2<=m'<=m and U_s subset V subset U_{s+t}. Modified comparison allows bounded w without requiring w<=0. At height h=s+t/2, the chosen threshold gives a=B_0 n^2 h epsilon^(-3)<1/128, hence q>31/32 and the claimed inverse bound (8/7)^n. The exact positive decomposition of omega_{(1-epsilon)w} gives C_H=[2(H+1)]^n(8/7)^n, independent of epsilon. Each U_s has positive capacity by individual strict-set positive volume and the constant test; this is not PVP.

The backwards iteration is valid without decreasing capacity continuity. Under its contradictory assumption, the geometric bound on the partial sums of t_j ensures s_{j+1}>0 before each application of the sublevel inequality. It then gives a(s_{j+1})<=a(s_j)/2, while s_j decreases to a strictly positive limit. Monotonicity contradicts positivity of the capacity there. The resulting lower bound is exactly D^n/(4^n C_H A). Combining it with the tail estimate gives the coarse potential bound. Combining it with Cap(X) gives a positive lower bound on ||F||_p, not on the total masses of arbitrary bounded potentials. Exclusion of the zero density uses only the previously audited individual nonzero-mass consequence.

The L1-to-uniform argument keeps epsilon, D, H and A independent of the sequence indices. Since m<=S, its inclusion U_{2D} subset {|u-v|>a/2} has the correct sign. The fixed positive lower capacity contradicts the thin-sublevel estimate followed by Holder and Chebyshev. Normalized L1 compactness supplies a subsequence, and its uniform limit is continuous and omega-psh. For normalized existence, positive smooth approximation is legitimate; Gauduchon AM-GM and A_j tending to A>0 bound c_j above. The density-norm lower bound and bounded ||f_j||_p bound c_j away from zero before any uniform potential bound is assumed. Uniform convergence and c_j f_j tending to c f in Lp justify the first passage to the limit by accepted bounded BT continuity.

For exponential solutions, absorbing the fixed smooth volume ratio preserves all hypotheses. Jensen with probability density A_j^(-1)f_j^(1/n)rho gives precisely lambda M_j<=n log(alpha/A_j)+(lambda/A_j) integral(-psi_j)f_j^(1/n)rho omega^n. Accepted normalized exponential integrability gives the required Lq control with q=np/(np-1). Thus the upper bound for M_j precedes, and does not depend on, the uniform potential estimate. The lower-density inequality c_p<=exp(lambda M_j)||f_j||_p gives the lower bound. The resulting uniform bounds permit simultaneous subsequences for M_j and psi_j. Uniform convergence makes exp(lambda u_j)f_j converge in Lp, and bounded BT continuity proves the exponential equation. Accepted bounded exponential comparison gives uniqueness even where f vanishes.

All dimension-one cases are valid: the normalized scalar identity is Stokes, rho=1 supplies the exponential trace, q=p/(p-1) is finite, and the capacity and comparison choices remain positive. Constants in the uniform estimates depend only on the stated fixed parameters and background; bounds for the approximation constants may also depend on the fixed nonzero density through A>0. No positive pointwise lower bound for the limiting density is required.

The comparison attributions match [KN15, Section 5 and Corollary 5.10](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1312.5491), [Dinew16, Section 6](https://www.numdam.org/article/AFST_2016_6_25_1_91_0.pdf), and [Nguyen16, Proposition 2.5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1501.00891). Their numerical normalizations and Nguyen's original normalized-existence-based lower bound are not imported. GZ17's local chapters are confirmed by the [publisher's contents](https://ems.press/books/etm/134/contents); the two local estimates remain explicitly accepted inputs. The supplied SGPT Chapter 2 was checked for bounded local products and test conventions, with its general big-class capacity distinguished from the present Hermitian capacity. No global Hermitian capacity estimate, Lp a priori theorem, weak existence result, BMP or PVP is assumed.
